title: Learn useful memories from evidence
subtitle: Extraction proposes claims; admission decides what to preserve.
purpose: Preserve useful meaning without inventing personal facts. Permitted sources remain searchable when extraction skips them.

steps.title: Read permitted input
steps.body: A background worker reads a source revision and justified context. Learning from live input waits until current controls resolve.

steps.title: Propose small claims
steps.body: Extract speaker, subject, scope, time, negation, uncertainty and exact support. Keep plans, beliefs and quotations qualified.

steps.title: Check support and policy
steps.body: Validate fields and evidence spans, compare related assertions, and apply versioned admission rules. Valid JSON does not establish truthful interpretation.

steps.title: Choose an outcome
steps.body: Add; apply a supported change; link independent evidence; record duplicate; preserve conflict; or reject. Rejected memories do not hide permitted sources.

steps.title: Commit safely
steps.body: Commit accepted claims and index jobs together. Record concise reasons and versions; reject stale worker attempts. Empty extraction differs from provider failure.

panels.title: What a candidate contains
items: Meaning: knowledge, an episode, or an authorized reusable procedure; primary category and optional labels.
Attribution: speaker, subject, and whether directly stated, inferred, summarized or observed.
Evidence: source ID, revision and exact span; dependencies allow correction and forgetting to invalidate interpretations.

panels.title: What must stay qualified
items: A wish is not an event; a promise is not completion; a quoted instruction is not current authority.
Do not infer preferences from visits, personal facts from fiction, or spelling preferences from ASR differences.
Ambiguous identity, date or scope remains unresolved. Record useful attribution instead of inventing missing details.

panels.title: Policy and proof
items: Greetings, repetition and boilerplate usually need no derived memory; source search still covers useful unclassified material.
Version prompts, model, admission rules and category registry. Model proposals cannot rewrite application permissions or policy.
Sensitive-information policy remains open; measure unsupported claims, wrong-person assignments and missed useful memories.

example: “My sister might visit Paris” supports the sister's tentative plan, not the user's visit or a completed trip. Keep her identity unresolved if unclear.
remaining: Unbuilt: worker, extraction contract, semantic checks and admission operations. Review remember/ignore/uncertain examples; test candidates against exact evidence.
mentor_question: What should Kivi remember automatically, and which uncertain or sensitive details need different treatment?
terms: Candidate = a proposed memory. Admission = deciding whether and how to save it. Attribution = who stated or experienced it. Dependencies = the source material that an interpretation relies on.

title: Keep people, time and changes distinct
subtitle: Every claim needs attribution, scope and time.
purpose: Connect history while preventing wrong-person merges, stale answers and unsupported replacement.

steps.title: Identify subject and scope
steps.body: Separate speaker from subject. Resolve people, projects, trips and tasks through evidence; a matching name is insufficient.

steps.title: Preserve meaning
steps.body: Keep actuality, intention, commitment, belief, condition and negation distinct. Store amounts with units and whether a limit is total or recurring.

steps.title: Preserve distinct clocks
steps.body: Separate event/validity time, source capture time and import availability. Missing dates remain unknown; late import does not imply recency.

steps.title: Compare related assertions
steps.body: Check subject, predicate, scope, time and supporting evidence. Distinguish a correction of an earlier mistake from a real-world change.

steps.title: Link or revise with evidence
steps.body: Link supported aliases and relationships; supersede only justified values. Preserve earlier history and unresolved alternatives; invalidate links when their evidence disappears.

panels.title: Identity and relationships
items: Entities, aliases and evidence-backed relationship links live in SQLite tables; no graph server is needed.
Every link inherits attribution, scope, polarity and time. A family role does not establish a work responsibility.
Keep unresolved mentions and reversible identity decisions. Application name is context, not proof of project identity.

panels.title: Lifecycle has two meanings
items: Claim state: active, disputed, superseded or excluded. These describe remembered knowledge.
Task state: planned, progressing, completed or blocked. Task completion differs from superseding a claim.
Repeated summaries of one source are not independent confirmation; retain original dependencies.

panels.title: Questions this enables
items: Current: What budget applies now? Historical: What budget applied before the change?
Attribution: Who promised to book? Confidence in identity must come from evidence, not identical names.
Conflict: Which statements disagree? Present alternatives when evidence cannot establish a replacement or shared identity.

example: Jaipur's total hotel budget changes from INR 6,000 to INR 8,000. Preserve the earlier value. Importing an older transcript tomorrow must not restore it as current; neither amount becomes a nightly limit.
remaining: Unbuilt: identity resolution, temporal comparison, revisions and link invalidation. Define replacement rules; test same-name people, pronouns, late records, negation and corrections.
mentor_question: What evidence should justify changing a value or merging two identities?

title: Find evidence sufficient for the question
subtitle: Search sources and memories; verify coverage before answering.
purpose: Recover meaning across records while preserving exact support, current controls and honest completeness limits.

steps.title: Define the read
steps.body: Use question, scope and relevant time. Apply trusted ownership, current exclusions and permitted-text rules to every retrieval route.

steps.title: Collect candidates
steps.body: Start with source keyword search. Optional hybrid search combines source/memory keyword lists with vector lists ranking meaning similarity.

steps.title: Combine and inspect
steps.body: Fuse ranked lists and deduplicate overlapping evidence. Read original supporting spans; follow bounded links or additional reads for missing bridge evidence.

steps.title: Check completeness
steps.body: Counts, complete lists and change histories require scoped enumeration plus source fallback for extraction gaps. Top-ranked matches alone cannot establish completeness.

steps.title: Pack the evidence bundle
steps.body: Preserve decisive excerpts, interpretations, IDs, revisions, conflicts and coverage within the token budget. Return readiness and a store-issued freshness token.

panels.title: Proposed budgets; unmeasured
items: 20 results per list; reciprocal-rank fusion combines list positions with k=60; keep at most 40 candidates.
Optional relationship expansion: one supported hop, at most 20 entities and 40 evidence references; indicate truncation.
4,096 evidence tokens using the actual tokenizer; reserve overhead and output. Enumeration starts at 100 records per page.

panels.title: Source fallback is essential
items: Unclassified text and records with empty or pending extraction remain recoverable through permitted source search.
Current exclusions govern source search, vectors, relationship expansion, full-history baselines and inspection equally.
Report conflicts and incomplete coverage; preserve original spans supporting personal-history claims.

panels.title: What needs comparison
items: Compare full permitted history, keyword sources, hybrid sources and hybrid plus typed memories on identical questions.
Local multilingual E5-small embeddings remain unproven here; test Hindi/Hinglish, names and negation.
Exact vector scoring avoids approximate-index losses; it does not guarantee semantic relevance, complete evidence or correct answers.

example: “What changed about Jaipur?” needs old and new budgets plus evidence connecting them to the same trip. A similar hotel preference cannot prove the change.
remaining: Unbuilt: keyword retrieval, evidence bundles, enumeration and freshness checks. Build source search first; justify vectors and relationship expansion through measured gains.
mentor_question: Which questions require exhaustive evidence, and what measured gain would justify vectors or relationship traversal?
terms: Keyword search matches words; vector search compares encoded meaning. Fusion combines ranked result lists. Tokens are the model’s text units. A freshness token records the knowledge versions used so publication can detect changes.

title: Apply context and handle uncertainty
subtitle: Answer, compare or draft using supported history.
purpose: Improve the present task while respecting current instructions, evidence gaps and the difference between drafting and doing.

steps.title: Start with the present task
steps.body: Identify the outcome: recover a promise, explain changes or prepare a draft. Do not insert personal history into ordinary dictation.

steps.title: Apply relevant context
steps.body: Use supported budgets, preferences and project details only when helpful. Retrieved facts need not be mentioned just because they exist.

steps.title: Honor current instructions
steps.body: Today's explicit request overrides remembered preferences for this run. A one-off override does not automatically become permanent.

steps.title: Select an honest response
steps.body: Enough evidence: answer. Unneeded unknown: omit. Material ambiguity: clarify. Missing evidence: state the gap and provide supported partial help.

steps.title: Publish an inspectable result
steps.body: Attach sources, label assumptions and distinguish drafts from observed outcomes. Recheck knowledge freshness and authority before accepting the response.

panels.title: When to ask or proceed
items: Ask one focused question when the answer depends on it. Reversible drafts may use explicitly labeled assumptions.
Skipped clarification is not confirmation. Preserve uncertainty and use the supported fallback.
Missing recipient, path, time or authority blocks dependent actions; prepare independently supported portions.

panels.title: Boundaries against invention
items: A visit does not prove enjoyment. Trip changes do not automatically reschedule meetings.
A file location does not establish contents or access. Remembered constraints do not establish live availability or a completed booking.
Historical instructions grant no current authority. Actual operation receipts establish successful effects.

panels.title: Evaluate usefulness and restraint
items: Measure supported task success, useful adaptation and unwanted personal callbacks; mentioning memory is not success.
Measure unsupported answers and unnecessary clarification/abstention across multilingual and ambiguous questions.
Self-reported model confidence is not calibrated certainty; examine evidence and consequences of missing details.

example: The user prefers short replies but requests a detailed Jaipur checklist today. Give detail using the latest supported budget and hotel preference. If no booked hotel appears in history, acknowledge the gap.
remaining: Unbuilt: response states, sources and task-quality evaluation. Define normal, ambiguous, corrected, forgotten and failed behavior in one journey.
mentor_question: What makes memory useful, and when should Kivi clarify rather than offer a partial draft?
